title: Section enrichment: decode JSON membership blob, expose section field on reminders and sections list on lists
description:
Sub-bead of **apple-reminders-mcp-rbf**. Depends on the DB reader scaffolding sub-bead.

# Scope

Surface within-list sections (the "kanban-style columns" introduced in Reminders 16+). EventKit does not expose these.

# Data model in DB

- **Section definitions**: `ZREMCDBASESECTION` (163 rows in user's DB). Columns: `Z_PK`, `Z_ENT` (5=BaseSection, 6=ListSection, 7=SmartListSection, 8=TemplateSection), `ZDISPLAYNAME`, `ZCANONICALNAME`, `ZCKIDENTIFIER` (UUID), `ZIDENTIFIER` (UUID bytes), and parent FKs `ZLIST` / `ZSMARTLIST` / `ZTEMPLATE`.
- **Reminder→section membership** is NOT a foreign key on the reminder. It is stored as a **JSON blob** on the parent list:
  - `ZREMCDBASELIST.ZMEMBERSHIPSOFREMINDERSINSECTIONSASDATA` (verified to start with `{"memberships":[{"modifiedOn":...`).
  - `ZREMCDBASELIST.ZSECTIONIDSORDERINGASDATA` — JSON blob with section ordering.
- **First task is to decode and document** the JSON shapes — the exact field names need verification against a real list. Hypothesized shape: `{"memberships": [{"sectionId": "<uuid>", "reminderIds": ["<uuid>", ...], "modifiedOn": <core-data-timestamp>}]}` but **must be confirmed**.

# Deliverables

- Section query helpers on `ReminderDBReader`:
  - `func sections(forListUUID: String) -> [SectionInfo]` returning `id`, `name`, `canonicalName`, ordered correctly per `ZSECTIONIDSORDERINGASDATA`
  - `func sectionForReminder(uuid: String) -> SectionInfo?` — looks up via the parent list's membership JSON
  - Batched variant for many reminders at once
- API model additions:
  - On reminder: `section: { id, name }?` — populated when the reminder is in a section, null otherwise
  - On list: `sections: [{id, name}]?` — populated when the list has sections, null when DB unavailable, `[]` when list has no sections
- CLI:
  - `reminders query --section <name>` filter (matches by section display name within the constraining list — must combine with `--list` to be unambiguous, OR accepts a section UUID)
  - `reminders lists --pretty` shows sections per list
- MCP:
  - `query_reminders` returns `section` field; accepts `sectionId` filter param
  - `get_lists` returns `sections` array

# Acceptance criteria

- [ ] **Membership JSON shape documented** in `docs/sqlite-schema-notes.md` (or similar) — sample blob, decoded structure, explanation of any unfamiliar fields
- [ ] Sections returned for a list match the ordering shown in Reminders.app
- [ ] Reminders in a sectioned list correctly resolve to their section
- [ ] Reminders not in any section have `section: null`
- [ ] Lists without sections return `sections: []`
- [ ] `--section` filter correctly scopes to matching reminders; passing an unknown section name when also providing `--list` errors clearly
- [ ] Tests verify section→reminder and reminder→section consistency on the fixture DB for at least 3 lists with sections
- [ ] Docs updated

# Risks / open questions

- Membership JSON format is not yet fully documented; the first deliverable in implementation order is to decode and pretty-print one to confirm the shape.
- If membership data is also stored in a place the section bead doesn't yet know about (e.g. a per-reminder column we missed), surface that finding before locking the API.
- Soft-deleted sections must be filtered (`ZMARKEDFORDELETION = 0`).
close_reason: Implemented per acceptance criteria

title: DB reader scaffolding: libsqlite3 wrapper, store discovery, schema fingerprint, FDA detection
description:
Sub-bead of **apple-reminders-mcp-rbf**.

# Scope

Create the foundational `ReminderDBReader` module that all subsequent enrichment work will build on. No user-visible fields yet — just the read-only access layer.

# Deliverables

- New file `Sources/AppleRemindersCore/ReminderDBReader.swift`
- Uses `import SQLite3` (system libsqlite3 from `Foundation` / `Darwin`) — **no new package dependencies**
- Public API (rough):
  - `ReminderDBReader.discover() -> [ReminderDBReader]` — finds and opens all relevant `Data-*.sqlite` stores in the group container
  - `init(storeURL: URL) throws` — opens with `SQLITE_OPEN_READONLY` flag (NOT `SQLITE_OPEN_READWRITE`), URI form `file://...?mode=ro`
  - `func schemaFingerprint() -> String` — hash of `Z_METADATA` + `Z_MODELCACHE` content; used to detect Apple schema changes
  - `func isSchemaSupported() -> Bool` — checks fingerprint against a known-good list
  - `func reminderRowID(forUUID uuid: String) -> Int64?` — helper for joining
  - Closes all sqlite connections in `deinit`
- Robust error type `ReminderDBError` with cases: `notFound`, `permissionDenied` (TCC/FDA), `unsupportedSchema(fingerprint)`, `sqliteError(code, message)`
- Permission detection: when `sqlite3_open_v2` fails with errno indicating TCC denial, surface `permissionDenied` so callers can degrade gracefully
- Logging: single stderr warning on first enrichment failure; suppress further warnings within the process

# Out of scope

- Any actual enrichment queries (hashtags, parents, sections) — those are separate sub-beads
- Caching — explicitly skipped per design
- Write paths — never

# Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `ReminderDBReader.discover()` returns one reader per live store, ignoring `Data-local.sqlite`, `*.sqlite-wal`, `*.sqlite-shm`
- [ ] All sqlite connections opened with `SQLITE_OPEN_READONLY | SQLITE_OPEN_NOMUTEX` and URI `mode=ro`. Verified by code review — no `SQLITE_OPEN_READWRITE` or `SQLITE_OPEN_CREATE` anywhere.
- [ ] On a system without FDA (or when the group container directory is unreadable), `discover()` returns `[]` and logs one stderr warning.
- [ ] Schema fingerprint is stable across reads (same DB → same fingerprint).
- [ ] At least one known-good fingerprint (current macOS Reminders schema) is recorded in code; unknown fingerprints log a clear warning naming the fingerprint and recommend filing an issue.
- [ ] Unit test: open the backed-up DB at `~/Dropbox/Backup/2026-05-08_04-28-49-apple-reminders-db-backup/sqlite-consistent-snapshots/Data-28F11402-…sqlite`; verify schema fingerprint, that ZREMCDREMINDER is queryable, that connection closes cleanly.
- [ ] No writes detectable: after running the test suite, the test DB's mtime is unchanged.

# Notes

- Use the URI form `file:<path>?mode=ro` not the bare-path form, to be explicit about read-only intent.
- WAL replay is required for current data — do **not** use `immutable=1`.
- `sqlite3_prepare_v3` with `SQLITE_PREPARE_PERSISTENT` is fine for hot statements, but not required.

title: Hashtag enrichment: per-reminder hashtags, --hashtag filter, list_hashtags tool
description:
Sub-bead of **apple-reminders-mcp-rbf**. Depends on the DB reader scaffolding sub-bead.

# Scope

Surface Apple Reminders hashtag data in both the CLI and MCP server. Hashtags are not exposed by EventKit at all today.

# Data model in DB

- **Master list**: `ZREMCDHASHTAGLABEL` rows (114 in user's DB). Columns of interest: `Z_PK`, `ZNAME`, `ZCANONICALNAME`, `ZACCOUNTIDENTIFIER`, `ZRECENCYDATE`, `ZFIRSTOCCURRENCECREATIONDATE`.
- **Per-reminder application**: `ZREMCDOBJECT` rows where `Z_ENT = 32` (REMCDHashtag). Each row has `ZHASHTAGLABEL` (FK to ZREMCDHASHTAGLABEL.Z_PK) and a reminder FK in one of `ZREMINDER` / `ZREMINDER1` / … / `ZREMINDER5`. In the current schema `ZREMINDER2` is the active column; query should `COALESCE` across the variants for forward-compat.

# Deliverables

- Hashtag query helper on `ReminderDBReader`:
  - `func hashtags(forReminderUUID: String) -> [String]`
  - `func hashtags(forReminderUUIDs: [String]) -> [String: [String]]` — batched join (use a single SQL with `IN (?, ?, ...)` to avoid N+1)
  - `func hashtagInventory() -> [HashtagInfo]` — returns full master list with usage counts
- API model addition: `hashtags: [String]?` on the public reminder model in `Models.swift` (use `null` when DB unavailable, `[]` when reminder has none)
- CLI:
  - `reminders query --hashtag <name>` filter (post-fetch JMESPath-equivalent — applied in Swift, not via JMESPath, to keep semantics clean)
  - New command `reminders hashtags [--pretty] [--all]` listing master hashtags with `name`, `canonicalName`, `usageCount`, `lastUsed`, `firstSeen`
- MCP:
  - `query_reminders` returns `hashtags` field
  - New tool `list_hashtags` mirroring the CLI command
  - Update tool descriptions / schemas

# Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Reminder output includes `hashtags: ["foo", "bar"]` when the reminder has hashtags, `[]` when it doesn't, and `null` when DB enrichment is unavailable
- [ ] Order of hashtags is stable across runs (sort by canonical name)
- [ ] `reminders query --hashtag work` returns only reminders tagged `#work` (case-insensitive on canonical name); works alongside other filters (e.g. `--list "Personal" --hashtag work`)
- [ ] `reminders hashtags` returns the master list; `--all` includes hashtags with zero current usage; default excludes them
- [ ] `list_hashtags` MCP tool produces equivalent JSON
- [ ] Tests against the fixture DB verify: known reminders have expected hashtags; aggregate counts match `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM ZREMCDOBJECT WHERE Z_ENT=32 AND ZMARKEDFORDELETION=0 GROUP BY ZHASHTAGLABEL`
- [ ] Docs updated: CLAUDE.md tools table; SKILL.md examples; new section in query-reference.md

title: Detect bulk modifiedDate touches from Apple Reminders list reorder
description:
Apple Reminders.app bumps the modifiedDate on every reminder in a list when you move one reminder between sections (or do similar list-level reorders). Repro: moved a single reminder between two sections in 'Task Journal' on 2026-05-10 at 17:54:03 PT, and all 1369 reminders in that list got the same modifiedDate timestamp.

Consequence: --modified-from filters and the SKILL recipe 'what did I complete recently?' return massive false-positive results after any section move. modifiedDate from EventKit is 'row written to disk', not 'user-visible content changed'.

Proposal:
1. Detect bulk-touch in query: if N>=50 reminders share a single modifiedDate (or even a 1s window), emit a single stderr warning naming the timestamp and the affected list(s), with a hint.
2. Optional CLI flag --exclude-bulk-touches on 'reminders query' that filters out reminders whose modifiedDate falls in a detected bulk-touch second (only when --modified-from/--modified-to are in use). Document why.

title: Parent/child enrichment: parentId and childIds on reminders, --parent / --top-level filters
description:
Sub-bead of **apple-reminders-mcp-rbf**. Depends on the DB reader scaffolding sub-bead.

# Scope

Surface the formal subtask hierarchy. EventKit nominally supports subtasks but our current API does not surface the parent/child link cleanly.

# Data model in DB

- `ZREMCDREMINDER.ZPARENTREMINDER` is an integer FK to the parent reminder's `Z_PK` (or NULL for top-level).
- 1,147 reminders in user's DB have a non-null `ZPARENTREMINDER`.
- UUIDs map directly via `ZCKIDENTIFIER` on both rows, so the join produces clean parent/child UUID pairs.

# Deliverables

- Parent/child helpers on `ReminderDBReader`:
  - `func parentUUID(forReminderUUID: String) -> String?`
  - `func childUUIDs(forReminderUUID: String) -> [String]`
  - Batched variants for both, returning `[String: String?]` and `[String: [String]]`
- API model additions on the reminder model:
  - `parentId: String?` (UUID of parent, null if top-level)
  - `childIds: [String]?` (UUIDs of direct children; null when DB unavailable; `[]` when none)
- CLI:
  - `reminders query --parent <id>` filter — returns only direct children of the given reminder UUID
  - `reminders query --top-level` filter — returns only reminders without a parent
  - These must compose with existing filters (`--list`, `--status`, etc.)
- MCP:
  - `query_reminders` accepts `parentId` and `topLevelOnly` boolean params with the same semantics
  - Tool description / schema updated

# Acceptance criteria

- [ ] When a reminder has a parent, `parentId` round-trips: looking up the reminder by `parentId` returns the parent reminder
- [ ] `childIds` is bidirectionally consistent: if reminder A's `childIds` includes B, then B's `parentId` is A
- [ ] `--top-level` and `--parent` are mutually exclusive at the CLI (validation error if both passed)
- [ ] `--parent <uuid>` returns 0 reminders cleanly when the parent has no children (not an error)
- [ ] Tests verify: known parent/child pairs from the fixture DB; round-trip consistency over a sample of 50 random parent/child pairs
- [ ] Docs updated

title: Decide final schema for DB-enriched fields (envelope flag vs nested object vs field omission)
description:
**Context**: The SQLite enrichment work (epic `apple-reminders-mcp-rbf`) added four DB-derived fields to `ReminderOutput`: `hashtags`, `parentId`, `childIds`, `section`. For the initial implementation we shipped the simplest disambiguation: a top-level `enriched: Bool` on the `query_reminders` response envelope. When `enriched: false`, the per-reminder DB fields are unset/null and should be treated as "unknown." When `enriched: true`, the per-reminder fields are authoritative — `null`/`[]` means "absent" or "none."

This bead captures the design alternatives we considered but deferred, to revisit once we have more usage data.

**Alternatives considered**:

1. **Top-level `enriched: Bool`** (shipped) — minimal, no per-reminder shape change, but caller must remember the envelope-level convention. Per-field nil-vs-unknown ambiguity is implicit.
2. **Nested `enriched: { hashtags, parentId, childIds, section }?` object** — explicit grouping, one null check covers everything. Self-documenting in JSON. Costs: deeper JSON paths (`reminders[].enriched.hashtags`), JMESPath migration, slight refactor of `Models.swift`. Easiest to extend with future DB-only fields (urgent alarms, rich text, smart lists).
3. **Field omission** — omit DB fields entirely when no DB access; present-but-null when DB access + no value. Pros: minimal shape change. Cons: absent-vs-null is a known footgun. Most JSON tooling (`jq`, Swift Codable, JS `obj.x === null`) collapses absent and null, making the distinction fragile to consumers.

**Inputs for the eventual decision**:
- How many DB-only fields exist by then? (More fields → nested grouping pays off more.)
- Are any fields hybrid EventKit/DB-derived? (parentId could plausibly come from EventKit subtask relationships — would naturally migrate to top-level.)
- Do downstream consumers (Claude Desktop, scripts, future TS clients) actually trip on the implicit envelope flag?
- JMESPath UX: do callers find themselves frequently writing `enriched && reminder.hashtags && ...`?

**When to act**: if/when we add a third DB-only field (e.g. urgent alarms), revisit the schema then. Earlier review is welcome if downstream usage exposes friction.

**Acceptance criteria for closing this bead**: a decision is recorded (either confirming the envelope-flag shape or migrating to nested/omission), with rationale captured in the response — and any migration steps executed if the decision is to change shape.

References in code:
- `Sources/AppleRemindersCore/RemindersManager.swift` — TODO comment near the response build
- `Sources/AppleRemindersCore/Models.swift` — `ReminderOutput` fields: `hashtags`, `parentId`, `childIds`, `section`

title: Extend MCP/CLI with EventKit-invisible fields via direct SQLite read (hashtags, parent/child, sections)
description:
# Goal

Extend the Apple Reminders MCP server and CLI to surface fields that EventKit does not expose, by reading the Reminders Core Data SQLite store directly in **read-only** mode alongside the existing EventKit access path.

The three target fields, in priority order:
1. **Hashtags** — biggest gap; full structured access (per-reminder list + master hashtag inventory)
2. **Parent/child relationships** — formal subtask hierarchy (1,147 child reminders in user's data)
3. **Sections** — within-list groupings (a.k.a. kanban-style columns introduced in Reminders 16+; 163 sections across user's lists)

# Non-goals

- No writes to the SQLite store. All mutations remain via EventKit.
- No replacement of EventKit. The DB layer is purely an enrichment read-through.
- No rich-text decoding (`ZTITLEDOCUMENT` / `ZNOTESDOCUMENT`) in this epic — deferred.
- No urgent-alarm decoding in this epic — deferred (would be a follow-on).
- No template / smart-list / sharee surfacing — deferred.

# Architecture

```
EventKit (authoritative; create/update/delete/notifications)
   │
   │ join by UUID (EKReminder.calendarItemIdentifier == ZCKIDENTIFIER)
   ▼
ReminderDBReader (read-only libsqlite3, opened with SQLITE_OPEN_READONLY)
   ├─ store discovery: ~/Library/Group Containers/group.com.apple.reminders/Container_v1/Stores/Data-*.sqlite
   ├─ schema fingerprint check (Z_METADATA / Z_MODELCACHE)
   ├─ tombstone filter (ZMARKEDFORDELETION = 0)
   └─ enrichment queries (hashtags, parents, sections)
```

# Key technical findings (already verified against live DB)

- **UUID join works**: `EKReminder.calendarItemIdentifier == ZCKIDENTIFIER == ZDACALENDARITEMUNIQUEIDENTIFIER`. Lossless EventKit↔DB mapping.
- **Hashtag link path**: `ZREMCDOBJECT` rows with `Z_ENT=32` (REMCDHashtag) join `ZHASHTAGLABEL → ZREMCDHASHTAGLABEL.Z_PK` and `ZREMINDER2 → ZREMCDREMINDER.Z_PK`. (ZREMINDER2 is the active column in current schema; need defensive handling for ZREMINDER/ZREMINDER1/3/4/5 across versions.)
- **Master hashtag list**: `ZREMCDHASHTAGLABEL` (ZNAME, ZCANONICALNAME, ZRECENCYDATE, ZFIRSTOCCURRENCECREATIONDATE).
- **Parent/child**: `ZREMCDREMINDER.ZPARENTREMINDER` is integer FK to parent's `Z_PK`. Self-join works directly. UUIDs round-trip via ZCKIDENTIFIER.
- **Sections**: `ZREMCDBASESECTION` table holds section definitions (ZDISPLAYNAME, ZCANONICALNAME, ZCKIDENTIFIER, ZLIST/ZSMARTLIST/ZTEMPLATE FK to parent). Reminder→section membership is stored as a **JSON blob** on the parent list: `ZREMCDBASELIST.ZMEMBERSHIPSOFREMINDERSINSECTIONSASDATA` (verified: starts with `{"memberships":[{"modifiedOn":...`). Decoding is straightforward.

# Permission model

The CLI/MCP binary itself does not need a special entitlement — Full Disk Access is **inherited from the calling terminal/process** for command-line tools. Document this clearly: when invoked from a terminal that has FDA, reads succeed; otherwise the binary should detect the permission error cleanly and degrade gracefully (warn once, return EventKit-only data).

# Implementation phases (sub-beads)

1. **DB reader scaffolding** — libsqlite3 wrapper, store discovery, schema fingerprint, FDA detection, tombstone-aware base query helpers
2. **Hashtag enrichment** — `hashtags: [String]` on reminders; `--hashtag` filter on query; `list_hashtags` tool/command
3. **Parent/child enrichment** — `parentId` and `childIds` on reminders; `--parent <id>` and `--top-level` filters
4. **Section enrichment** — JSON membership decoder; `section: {id, name}?` on reminders; `sections: [...]` on lists
5. **Surface integration & tests** — wire fields through `Models.swift`, `RemindersManager`, MCP tool definitions, CLI flags; integration tests against a test fixture DB; docs

# Field naming convention

DB-only enrichment fields land directly on the existing reminder/list output schemas (no `ext.` prefix). Rationale: they're first-class data from the user's perspective — a hashtag isn't a debug detail. Where a field overlaps with EventKit (e.g. parent), prefer the DB-derived value when present and fall through to EventKit otherwise.

# Acceptance criteria for the epic

- [ ] Running `reminders query --pretty` (when terminal has FDA) returns `hashtags`, `parentId`, `childIds`, and `section` fields populated for reminders that have them.
- [ ] `reminders lists --pretty` returns `sections` array per list when sections exist.
- [ ] New `reminders hashtags` command lists the hashtag inventory with usage counts.
- [ ] New `--hashtag <name>` and `--parent <id>` / `--top-level` filters work on `reminders query`.
- [ ] MCP tools (`query_reminders`, `get_lists`, plus a new `list_hashtags`) expose the same fields.
- [ ] When run from a terminal **without** FDA: enrichment is silently disabled, EventKit-only data is returned, a single stderr warning is logged on first attempt.
- [ ] When the SQLite schema fingerprint is unrecognized: enrichment is disabled with a stderr warning naming the unknown fingerprint, EventKit-only data is returned.
- [ ] Existing tests pass; new tests cover the enrichment paths against a fixture DB.
- [ ] Docs (CLAUDE.md, SKILL.md, query-reference.md) updated with the new fields and commands.
- [ ] No writes to the live or any SQLite store — verified by code review (only `SQLITE_OPEN_READONLY` opens).

# Open questions to resolve during implementation

- How to handle multiple `Data-*.sqlite` files: which store maps to which EventKit source? Tentative: load all stores; when joining by UUID, the right store will simply have the row. Skip `Data-local.sqlite` (legacy, dormant since 2023).

title: Snapshot system: include enriched SQLite fields (hashtags, parentId, childIds, section, list sections)
description:
The git-backed snapshot currently writes only EventKit-derived fields. The SQLite enrichment layer (hashtags, parentId, childIds, section on reminders; sections on lists) is NOT persisted to snapshots. This means snapshots are lossy w.r.t. data visible elsewhere in the tool — hashtags, parent/child links, and section assignments are absent from per-reminder JSON files and lists.json.

Locations:
- SnapshotManager.convertToSnapshotOutput() builds SnapshotReminderOutput, which lacks hashtags/parentId/childIds/section fields (Sources/AppleRemindersCore/SnapshotManager.swift:466-510, struct at :524-539).
- SnapshotManager.takeSnapshot() builds ReminderListOutput directly from calendars (:69-75), bypassing RemindersManager.getAllLists() which already enriches with sections.
- SnapshotManager.takeSnapshot() calls store.fetchReminders() directly (:59-64), returning bare Reminder model objects without enrichment.

Plan:
1. Add hashtags/parentId/childIds/section to SnapshotReminderOutput.
2. SnapshotManager should accept dbReaders (mirror RemindersManager constructor); call the readers after fetchReminders to enrich.
3. Build lists.json with sections when enrichment is available.
4. Bump SnapshotState.currentSchemaVersion 2 -> 3 to force a full re-export on first run.
5. When enrichment is unavailable (no Full Disk Access), write nulls — same convention as the live query path; emit a single stderr warning at most.
6. Wire dbReaders through CLI SnapshotCommand and MCP auto-snapshot paths.
7. Decide section serialization shape — likely the existing SectionInfo Codable.
8. Add a test using the existing jtest1 SQLite fixture verifying that a snapshot of a list with sections + hashtags writes the new fields.

title: JMESPath: register lower() and upper() custom functions
